A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RadGPT and AbdomenAtlas 3.0. Their main texts, algorithms, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across the substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original tumor-detection benchmarks, pancreatic staging results, radiologist evaluation of tumor measurements, and validation of LLM report labeling.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and adds internal validation, additional report-generation baselines, and RadGraph-F1 results.

M1.justification: The segmentation-to-report pipeline, organ sub-segmentation, tumor measurement and staging algorithms, post-processing, and LLM prompts remain substantively unchanged. Appendix Algorithms 1–4 match across versions. The expanded radiologist-review description documents existing safeguards rather than establishing a new RadGPT procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions retain 9,262 scans from the same 17 source datasets, the same organ-focused tasks, and 240 combined human–AI reports. However, the reported institution count changes from 88 to 138 without corresponding changes to source-dataset institution counts or an explanation of new sources. The PDFs do not resolve whether hospital coverage expanded or a summary statistic was corrected. The added IID evaluation principally changes the split.

E2.justification: v1 evaluates CT2Rep and M3D against RadGPT. v2 adds CT-CHAT, Merlin, and RadFM to the detection and report-metric comparisons, substantially broadening the comparator set. The main-table head-to-head comparison for CRC liver metastases is removed, although RadGPT's metastasis threshold analysis remains in the appendix.

E3.justification: v2 implements the previously proposed random 10% AbdomenAtlas test split and reports IID alongside external evaluation. It adds RadGraph-F1 using RadGraph-XL and training protocols for CT-CHAT and Merlin. Table 2 also changes the reported external large-pancreatic-tumor count from 105 to zero; this revision is not reconciled with the retained threshold plot. Existing CT2Rep settings and RadGPT thresholds remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The existing report-style sensitivity analysis is extended to RadGraph-F1 in Appendix B.3. New Appendix C supplies a qualitative error analysis describing unsupported findings in generated reports and their identification during review. Threshold sensitivity curves and the appendix's illustrated clinical cases are retained rather than newly added analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates for benchmark performance. Revised sample counts and additional point estimates do not change statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: v2 adds the IID results matrix and three baselines' results, revises M3D and text-metric scores, and removes large-pancreatic and CRC-metastasis comparisons from Table 2. Table 1 changes annotated liver/pancreas/kidney case totals from 929/344/1,674 to 1,472/361/2,122; appendix distributions also change. Table 3 revises measurement accuracy from 93.8% to 93.5%. Retained RadGPT UCSF liver, kidney, and small-pancreatic detection scores remain unchanged; the revisions do not establish a same-setting RadGPT performance gain.

T1.justification: Neither version introduces theoretical propositions or proofs. The mathematical operations and rules in Algorithms 1–4, including measurement and staging thresholds, are unchanged. Adding an empirical RadGraph-F1 evaluation does not introduce new mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The principal contributions remain the annotated abdominal CT dataset and segmentation-assisted report generation. v2 narrows the abstract's broad first image-text 3D medical dataset claim to high-quality abdominal CT reports, explicitly claims release of the intermediate AbdomenAtlas 2.0 dataset, and adds a claim of faster report creation than traditional human reporting. The dataset-first emphasis mostly reframes retained contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly interprets imperfect automated staging as evidence that radiologist revision is essential. Appendix B.3 also acknowledges that BERT and RadGraph-F1 rankings do not align with diagnostic accuracy, replacing v1's statement that RadGPT leads every reported text metric. The new discussion expands the interpretability and human-interaction rationale while retaining the original segmentation-based explanation.

D1.justification: Appendix B.1 adds substantial CT-CHAT and Merlin implementation information, including preprocessing, model connections, training schedules, and CT-CHAT's four A100 GPUs and batch size. Appendix C documents mask correction, iterative consistency checks, escalation to radiologists, and report comparison. Conversely, v1's explicit identification of SuPreM for organ segmentation is dropped. These are documentation changes, not evidence that RadGPT itself changed.

R1.justification: The data-scarcity positioning remains, but v2 adds CT-CHAT, RadFM, RadGraph-related references, and discussion of chest X-ray report generators while removing several broader biomedical references. It explains the restriction to CT comparators, updates Merlin from unreleased to partially released, acknowledges its RadGraph evaluation, and clarifies the relationship among AbdomenAtlas versions.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around dataset creation, with an explicit contribution list. Experimental subsections are reorganized, diagnostic-metric discussion moves into Appendix B.3, and new discussion and radiologist-review sections are introduced. Fusion reports become enhanced human reports, alongside substantial prose, author-list, and acknowledgment edits.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially redesigned into IID/OOD blocks; Table 3 is transposed and condensed. v2 adds a staging illustration and a table summarizing the existing human-report audit, while moving and expanding the text-metric table into the appendix. Confusion matrices are redrawn and distribution plots are revised and rearranged. The pipeline image and most clinical-example images remain identical.

improvement.justification: The completed IID benchmark, broader CT comparator set, RadGraph evaluation, and explicit radiologist-review documentation make v2 more informative and reproducible. The revised interpretation also acknowledges metric disagreements and the need for human correction. These gains are tempered by unexplained cohort and provenance revisions, particularly Table 2 reporting no external large pancreatic tumors while Figure 15 retains results for them. The evidence supports a limited net improvement.
